latest_release.name: PyTorch 2.15.0 Release
latest_release.body:
# PyTorch 2.15.0 Release Notes - [Highlights](#highlights) - [Backwards Incompatible Changes](#backwards-incompatible-changes) - [Deprecations](#deprecations) - [New Features](#new-features) - [Improvements](#improvements) - [Bug fixes](#bug-fixes) - [Performance](#performance) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Security](#security) - [Developers](#developers) # Highlights
Rewritten NCCL backend becomes the default, with a flight recorder that dumps on hangs and TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0 or nccl-legacy as rollback paths
One-sided transports for torch.distributed, with a NIXL backend and CUDA-graph-capturable transfers
FSDP2 and pipelining gain finer memory and communication control, with fp32 for precision-sensitive parameters, CUDA-graph-captured gradient accumulation, and gradient reduction overlapped with compute
Faster 4-bit (NVFP4) LLM decoding on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs through fewer, better-overlapped kernel launches in NVGEMM
Apple Silicon gains FP8 and faster decode, with float8_e4m3fn and _scaled_mm, a new grouped_mm with a decode fast path (1.32–1.34x tokens/s on MoE decode), and public torch.mps.Stream APIs
Broader platform support with FlyDSL kernels on AMD gfx950, Tensor Data Mover support for gfx1250 (MI450), ROCm 10.0 wheels, simpler SYCL kernel authoring and multi-GPU profiling on Intel GPUs, CUDA 13.2 as the default wheel with CUDA 13.4 alongside it, and torch.compile on Python 3.15
For more details about these highlighted features, you can look at the release blogpost. Below are the full release notes for this release. # Backwards Incompatible Changes ## Python Frontend ### `import torch` can no longer be re-executed in the same process, including via `importlib.reload(torch)` (#194654) `importlib.reload(torch)` and `del sys.modules["torch"]` + re-import now raise, as does retrying `import torch` after it failed. Re-running the module body was already unsafe in exactly the same way as the retry, so the new check does not distinguish the two. Normal use is unaffected: a successful import leaves `torch` in `sys.modules` so the body never re-runs, and re-entrant imports from a backend extension during autoload still short-circuit on `sys.modules` without reaching the check. Version 2.14: ```python import importlib import torch importlib.reload(torch) # RuntimeError: Only a single TORCH_LIBRARY can be used to register the namespace triton; ... # (re-importing after a failed `import torch` failed with similarly misleading errors or could segfault) ``` Version 2.15: ```python import importlib import torch importlib.reload(torch) # ImportError: `torch` can only be initialized once per process, so this module cannot # be imported again: neither via `importlib.reload(torch)`, nor by re-importing after # a failed `import torch`. ``` ### Nested tensors are no longer allowlisted for `torch.load(..., weights_only=True)` (#194380) Nested jagged and strided nested tensors are no longer on the default `weights_only` allowlist. Loading a checkpoint that contains one with `weights_only=True` (the default) now fails with `Unsupported global: GLOBAL torch.nested._internal.nested_tensor._rebuild_njt was not an allowed global by default` (or `GLOBAL torch._utils._rebuild_nested_tensor` for strided nested tensors). To load checkpoints containing nested tensors, allow them explicitly with `torch.serialization.safe_globals` (see below), or use `weights_only=False` for trusted files. Version 2.14: ```python loaded = torch.load("njt.pt", weights_only=True) # works ``` Version 2.15: ```python from torch.nested._internal.nested_tensor import _rebuild_njt, NestedTensor with torch.seriali
